ai.note: Design note: the six great powers use the weights tuned for the Spain scenario. The smaller states put no value on ground outside their own, so they defend and recruit but do not attack; the Serbian rising may.

unitTypes.name: Line infantry division
unitTypes.note: Design note: the baseline the other types are measured against. A division of foot; it may march where there is no road.

unitTypes.name: Light infantry brigade
unitTypes.note: Design note: skirmishers and rifles. Cheaper in men and quicker to raise than the line, with less staying power.

unitTypes.name: Grenadier division
unitTypes.note: Design note: picked men grouped for the assault.

unitTypes.name: Guard infantry
unitTypes.note: Design note: the Imperial, Russian, Prussian and British guards. The best foot on the map, slow and dear to replace.

unitTypes.name: Militia and landwehr
unitTypes.note: Design note: needs no building, trains in a turn and finishes even in contested ground; cheap in Funds and dear in men.

unitTypes.name: Janissaries
unitTypes.note: Design note: fierce in attack and loose in defence beside European line infantry.

unitTypes.name: Light cavalry brigade
unitTypes.note: Design note: hussars, chasseurs and uhlans. Mobile: an all-cavalry force rides up to two territories by road.

unitTypes.name: Heavy cavalry division
unitTypes.note: Design note: cuirassiers and carabiniers. Their charge adds to the attack roll on firm ground.

unitTypes.name: Cossacks
unitTypes.note: Design note: cheap, quick to raise, and mobile; no match for formed troops.

unitTypes.name: Foot artillery
unitTypes.note: Design note: a reserve park. Adds to the attack roll beside other troops and never attacks alone; its guns need a road.

unitTypes.name: Horse artillery
unitTypes.note: Design note: guns that keep up with cavalry.

unitTypes.name: General
unitTypes.note: U5: adds to the battle roll of the army he is with and rallies its demoralized units.

unitTypes.name: Great captain
unitTypes.note: Design note: Napoleon in person, worth twice another general's command. Replacements are ordinary generals.

factions.name: French Empire
factions.motivation: Break the coalition before it can unite, and make Paris the capital of Europe.

briefing.objective: Master the Continent. You hold France, Belgium, the Rhine, Piedmont, the Kingdom of Italy and Hanover, with the Grande Armée gathered at Boulogne facing England. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Scouts report Mack's Austrians massing in Upper Austria and Kutuzov's Russians marching through Volhynia, still weeks behind. The Grande Armée stands on the Channel, ready to cross or to turn. Does it wait for the fleets, or march for the Rhine and the Danube?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: United Kingdom
factions.motivation: Keep the Continent divided and the seas open to British trade.

briefing.objective: Deny Europe to any one master. You hold the British Isles, Gibraltar and Malta, and the ports to land where you choose. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: The camps around Boulogne are breaking up, and agents in Hanover say the garrison there is thin. General Craig's corps waits at Malta. Do we land in northern Germany, help Naples, or keep the army at home until the Channel is safe?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Kingdom of Prussia
factions.motivation: Enlarge the kingdom of Frederick the Great while the other powers exhaust themselves.

briefing.objective: Lead northern Germany. You hold Brandenburg, Silesia, East and South Prussia and Westphalia, with a rested army between France and Russia. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Both sides court Berlin. Bernadotte's corps in Hanover lies between our provinces, and the Saxon court has no army to speak of. Do we strike for Hanover, take Saxony, or keep the army watching the Vistula?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Russian Empire
factions.motivation: Carry the Tsar's authority to the Danube, the Baltic and the Straits.

briefing.objective: Make Russia the arbiter of Europe. You hold the lands from Finland's border to Georgia, and the Ionian Islands far to the south. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Kutuzov's army stands at the Galician frontier and Buxhoeveden's and Bennigsen's corps gather behind it. The Ottoman forts on the Dniester are weakly held. Do the columns march west to meet the French, or south to the Danube?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Austrian Empire
factions.motivation: Recover Italy and Germany from the French.

briefing.objective: Restore the house of Habsburg. You hold Austria, Bohemia, Hungary, Galicia, Tyrol and Venetia, between France, Prussia, Russia and the Sultan. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Mack's army is ready on the Inn, the Bavarians are still undecided in Munich, and Archduke Charles faces Masséna across the Adige. The Grande Armée is far off on the Channel coast. Does the main blow fall on Bavaria or on Italy?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Ottoman Empire
factions.motivation: Hold the Sultan's provinces together and recover the Black Sea coast.

briefing.objective: Restore the Sultan's rule. You hold the Balkans, Anatolia, Syria and Egypt, but Serbia has risen and the Tsar's garrisons stand on the Black Sea. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Karageorge's rebels hold the hills south of Belgrade, the citadel's garrison holds out, and Russian troops are drilling along the Dniester. Do we crush the Serbs first, or strengthen Bender and the Danube forts?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Kingdom of Spain
factions.motivation: Keep the Bourbon crown whole between France and the sea.

briefing.objective: Guard the Peninsula. You hold Spain, the Balearics and the client kingdom in Tuscany, allied to a France you cannot refuse. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: The combined fleet lies at Cádiz with a British squadron outside. Do we garrison the ports, or send the regiments to the Pyrenees?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Kingdom of Portugal
factions.motivation: Stay independent of both Madrid and Paris.

briefing.objective: Keep Lisbon free. You hold Portugal's two regions and its oldest alliance is with Britain. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Spanish regiments are drilling beyond Badajoz. Do we mass at Elvas, or hold the line of the Tagus?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Batavian Republic
factions.motivation: Keep Holland's trade and canals out of the war.

briefing.objective: Guard the delta. You hold the Netherlands, with France on one side and the Royal Navy on the other. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Marmont's corps has left its Dutch camps for the Rhine. Do we watch the coast, or the eastern frontier?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Denmark and Norway
factions.motivation: Keep the Sound and the twin kingdoms neutral.

briefing.objective: Hold the Sound. You hold Denmark, Holstein and Norway, and every power wants your fleet. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: British sails have been counted off the Skagerrak, and the army stands in Holstein. Should the garrison of Copenhagen be strengthened?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Kingdom of Sweden
factions.motivation: Hold Finland and Pomerania against stronger neighbours.

briefing.objective: Defend the north. You hold Sweden, Finland and Swedish Pomerania, with Russia across one border and Prussia near another. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Stralsund's garrison asks for reinforcements, and so does Sveaborg. Which fortress comes first?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Electorate of Bavaria
factions.motivation: Survive between Vienna and Paris, and come out a kingdom.

briefing.objective: Keep Bavaria whole. You hold Munich, Ulm, the Upper Palatinate and Würzburg, with Austria's army at the border. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Austrian columns are gathering on the Inn. Do we hold Munich, or draw the army back toward Würzburg?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Württemberg and Baden
factions.motivation: Keep the Swabian courts standing while armies cross their land.

briefing.objective: Hold the Upper Rhine. You hold Württemberg and Baden, on the road from Strasbourg to Ulm. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Couriers say the French will ask for passage. Do we guard Stuttgart, or the crossings of the Rhine?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Hessian States
factions.motivation: Keep the Hessian purse and regiments out of other men's wars.

briefing.objective: Guard the road from the Main to the Weser. You hold Kassel and Frankfurt. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: French corps at Mainz and Hanover lie on either side of us. Which road should be watched?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Electorate of Saxony
factions.motivation: Stay out of the war that Prussia and Austria may fight over Saxony.

briefing.objective: Hold the Elbe. You hold Dresden, Leipzig and Thuringia between Berlin and Prague. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Prussian hussars have been seen near the Elbe. Do we hold Dresden, or Leipzig?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Swiss Confederation
factions.motivation: Keep every army out of the cantons.

briefing.objective: Hold the passes. You hold the nineteen cantons, astride every road from Germany to Italy. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Austrian posts in Vorarlberg and French ones in Valais are both being reinforced. Which frontier should the militia watch?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Papal States
factions.motivation: Keep Rome and the Holy See independent.

briefing.objective: Guard Rome. You hold Lazio, Umbria and the Marches. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: French officers have been asking about the harbor at Ancona. Should its garrison be doubled?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Kingdom of Naples
factions.motivation: Keep both shores of the Strait of Messina for the Bourbons.

briefing.objective: Hold the Two Sicilies. You hold Naples and Sicily, with the British at Malta and the French to the north. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: A British and Russian landing has been promised, and the French have noticed. Do we hold the Abruzzi, or keep the army at Naples?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Kingdom of Sardinia
factions.motivation: Keep the island, and hope for Piedmont.

briefing.objective: Keep the House of Savoy alive. You hold the island of Sardinia. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Corsican privateers are active in the straits. Which harbor should the garrison watch?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Barbary Regencies
factions.motivation: Keep Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli free to tax the sea.

briefing.objective: Hold the African shore. You hold Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli under the Sultan's distant name. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Foreign frigates have been seen off Tripoli and Algiers. Which harbor is most in danger?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Sultanate of Morocco
factions.motivation: Keep the Sultan's coast closed to foreign armies.

briefing.objective: Hold the Moroccan plains. You hold Fez, Tangier and Marrakesh. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: Ships from Gibraltar and Cádiz pass the strait daily. Should Tangier be reinforced?

factions.note: Design note: starting treasury, objectives and color are for play.

factions.name: Serbian Rising
factions.motivation: Drive the garrisons out and win Serbia its own rule.

briefing.objective: Free Serbia. You hold the Šumadija and must take Belgrade and Nish to keep it. Win by holding 42 of 105 territories or 52 of 103 cities.
briefing.firstTurnHint: The garrison of Belgrade is short of bread, and an army is gathering at Nish. Which do we face first?

development.name: Farmland
development.note: Design note: the land feeds and fills the regiments. Yields are first guesses, sized so a great power raises about a division a turn.

development.name: Trade
development.note: Design note: markets, mines and shipping.

development.name: Manufactories
development.note: Design note: foundries, mills and tailors' shops; each level allows one more Recruit order a turn in its territory.

buildings.name: Barracks
buildings.note: Design note: needed for regular troops.

buildings.name: Gun foundry
buildings.note: Design note: needed for guns and the guard.

buildings.name: Remount depot
buildings.note: Design note: needed for heavy cavalry and horse artillery.

buildings.name: Supply depot
buildings.note: Design note: magazines make replacing losses a quarter cheaper; needed for grenadiers and the guard.

buildings.name: Fortress
buildings.note: Design note: a walled place takes 2 off the attacker's roll.

buildings.name: Military hospital
buildings.note: Design note: raises the most men a unit may replace in a turn.

improvements.note: Design note: there are no railways in 1805. The rules need a rail entry, but no sub-territory may build one.

recruitment.note: Design note: carried over from the Spain scenario.

movement.note: Design note: two armies a turn for each port level.

d20.note: Design note: the battle table and its numbers are carried over from the Spain scenario until they are tuned for this one.

weather.note: Design note: tables are estimates by climate; they run from the best weather to the worst. Severe cold costs a marching army 8 percent of its men.

air.note: Design note: there are no aircraft in 1805. This block is here because generals (death, rally and replacement) run in the same rules module; generalDeathRoll is the only number used.
